transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2029-12-09
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Luca Romano (Redwood CSM); Evan Park (DeltaCore Head of Partnerships); Marina Liu (DeltaCore Senior Cloud Engineer); Sanjay Patel (DeltaCore GPU Infrastructure Lead); Olivia Chen (DeltaCore Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
DeltaCore is exploring a partner integration with Redwood to offer Redwood inference as a managed onramp inside DeltaCore's cloud marketplace and as an optional dedicated GPU-reselling channel. Key concerns: VPC/private deployment options, KMS/HSM integration, latency SLAs for inferencing, and marketplace billing flow. Agreed to run baseline throughput tests and exchange network/compliance artifacts.

Topics:
- Partner marketplace integration (billing, onboarding)
- Dedicated vs hosted routing and pricing bands
- Network peering, VPC, and private control plane
- Security: KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2
- Pilot scope, timeline, success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for hopping on. quick intro, i'm jordan miles from redwood inference, i'm the AE on the partner motion
[00:08] Evan: hi, evan here. thanks. excited to talk through how we might bring redwood into delta core marketplace. we're calling it a managed inference onramp
[00:15] Priya: thanks evan. i'm priya, solutions engineer. we typically look at three patterns — hosted api, dedicated capacity and private vpc. curious which you're leaning towards
[00:26] Marina: for our customers most will want a marketplace simple call where delta bills them, but we also have enterprise customers that need private vpc and kms. so both actually
[00:38] Sanjay: yeah, and we have strict p99 latency targets for our realtime agents — around 120ms at batch size 1 for our 8k seq models. that's the big technical ask
[00:50] Priya: okay that's helpful. 120ms p99 at single token is aggressive but we can get there with optimized kernels and GPU packing; the question is node sizing and whether we use quantized 4-bit vs 8-bit
[01:05] Evan: also the billing flow — we don't want customers double billed. delta handles marketplace billing and pays partners downstream. can redwood support marketplace metering or do we have to do a pass-through
[01:15] Jordan: great question. we support partner metering integrations today — there is a marketplace billing API and also reseller invoices. we'll send the integration doc but you'll likely want the partner metering route
[01:28] Olivia: on security side we need to know about key management — our customers require HSM-backed KMS, separation of customer keys, and long-term audit logs retained for 3 years. can redwood support that
[01:40] Priya: we've done HSM/KMS integrations with customer-managed keys in our private deployments, and we surface audit logs through the console and can ship to customer s3 or syslog. we'll validate retention windows
[01:55] Luca: quick note, for enterprise we also offer dedicated pools — customers can have reserved capacity that delta could resell. that reduces variability
[02:05] Marina: hypothetically how would a canary rollout look? enterprise customers want canary first to reduce risk
[02:12] Priya: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if a node goes unhealthy. it is handled by our routing layer — but on private deployments we need a small control plane connection back to redwood
[02:26] Sanjay: small control plane is acceptable, but we need to understand the exact egress/ingress endpoints and certs — security can't allow random outbound connections
[02:36] Jordan: we'll provide a network diagram and exact fqdn list. evan, can you share ip ranges and your peering model after the call
[02:45] Evan: yes, i'll send that today. also, we have an integration checklist for marketplace partners that includes SSO, product listing metadata, and invoices — we'll share
[02:55] Priya: perfect. on perf, would you be able to share a sample model and typical request distribution — sequence length, tokens per request — so we can simulate
[03:05] Marina: yes, we'll send a sample 8k model and a small corpus. note that our customers use both streaming and non-streaming, streaming is important
[03:15] Priya: streaming's supported. for 8k models streaming latency is sensitive to kv-cache evictions; we'll tune caching vs memory pressure
[03:28] Sanjay: curious about quantization — are there recommended quant profiles for our hardware? we plan to use A100 equivalents but with mixed gen fleets
[03:38] Priya: we have suggested quant profiles. for A100-class we recommend int8 for latency-critical, but 4-bit with compilers can be great for cost. mySE note: int4 can sometimes regress quality; we'll run evals
[03:55] Olivia: and on compliance, do you provide SOC2/ISO docs? our procurement needs that before we list a partner
[04:02] Jordan: yes we have SOC2 and ISO artifacts; we'll share our compliance pack. for customers requiring on-prem air-gapped installs we have an on-prem package though it takes a bit longer
[04:15] Evan: timeline wise, delta wants a pilot in january — lightweight 6 week pilot with 50-200 daily active customers. is that feasible
[04:24] Priya: feasible. sequence: share artifacts, run baseline perf in our infra or yours, then pilot. baseline can be done in two weeks if we get samples
[04:35] Sanjay: do you have a prescriptive network peering guide? we need MTU, port ranges, and firewall rules
[04:42] Priya: yes i'll attach our network guide. also note some customers have had weird issues with tcp idle timeouts on certain load balancers — we call that out
[04:55] Marina: what's the support model during pilot? SLA? engineer on-call?
[05:01] Luca: during pilots we assign a solutions engineer and an on-call runbook; enterprise pilots can have a 24/7 escalation channel as add-on
[05:12] Evan: what's the commercial split? marketplace fee then delta pays redwood? are you open to revenue share for the first 12 months
[05:22] Jordan: we are open to a marketplace revenue share for partner onboarding. need to route to commercial but initial terms are flexible for strategic partners
[05:35] Olivia: any red flags we should know — data residency or EU customers
[05:41] Priya: we support region pinning; for EU we can keep inference in EU regions and with dedicated private planes
[05:48] Evan: ok great. can we do a technical deep dive next week focused on private deployment networking and KMS with your infra team
[05:56] Jordan: yes, we'll set up a 90-minute deep dive. i'll include our private deployment lead. how about dec 16
[06:02] Evan: works for us
[06:05] Jordan: recap — redwood to share integration diagram, compliance pack, network guide; delta to send VPC topology and sample model. we'll run a perf baseline and reconvene on 12/16 for deep dive
[06:20] Olivia: thanks everyone
[06:22] Marina: thanks
[06:25] [end]

Notes on transcription: some words may be auto-corrected; 'Redwood Dedicated' appears as 'redwood dedicate' in a couple spots; 'KV cache' transcribed as 'k v cache' in a couple places
